recession_scenario.evidence: Recession stress test assumes 2% GDP contraction (moderate recession), 28% revenue decline based on 2022-2023 semiconductor downturn. Operating margin compression of 800bps due to operating deleverage. EPS decline of 52% vs revenue decline of 28% demonstrates operating leverage. Stock price impact of 38% based on historical recession drawdowns. Recovery timeline 9-12 months typical for semiconductor cycles. Balance sheet strength (net cash) supports recession navigation without distressed capital raising.

competitive_market_share_loss.evidence: Competitive scenario assumes NVIDIA maintains 85%+ AI accelerator share through 2027, limiting AMD to 10% vs 15% base case. Data center GPU revenue impact of $6B (15% of revenue). Margin pressure from competitive pricing reduces operating margin by 200bps. EPS impact of 28% reflects margin compression. Stock multiple compression to 28x forward P/E (vs 31.7x) creates 32% stock price impact. Scenario reflects CUDA ecosystem moat persistence.

supply_chain_disruption.evidence: Supply chain stress test assumes Taiwan conflict creates 6-month TSMC supply disruption. Revenue impact of 45% reflects lost production and customer allocation. Earnings impact of 72% includes operating deleverage and expediting costs. Stock price impact of 55% reflects systemic semiconductor risk. Recovery timeline 12-18 months as TSMC Arizona capacity ramps. Probability of 15% based on geopolitical assessments. Existential risk requiring portfolio-level diversification.

interest_rate_shock.evidence: Interest rate stress test assumes Fed hikes to 6% in inflation shock scenario. Revenue impact of 8% from reduced enterprise IT spending. Minimal earnings impact due to net cash position (no interest expense increase). Stock price impact of 28% driven by multiple compression to 24x forward P/E from current 31.7x. WACC increases to 10.2% from 8.7%, reducing DCF valuation by $28 per share. Probability of 20% based on inflation reacceleration risk.

aggregate_stress_analysis.evidence: Worst case combines recession (30% probability) with competitive market share loss (40% probability), yielding 12% joint probability. Revenue decline of 38% and earnings decline of 68% from combined effects. Stock price impact of 52% (target price $78) reflects multiple compression and earnings decline. Balance sheet remains solid with net cash providing 24 months of operating expense coverage. Company remains viable with path to recovery in 18-24 months.
